maria: Heads-up — after last night's rollout the draft-matchmaker flow shows a 3x p95 increase when pairing mixtral-v2 drafts with qwen-lite finalizer. Noticed KV cache miss rate jumped ~40%. @ash can you triage? :eyes:
ash: on it. do you have a small repro or a trace?
maria: repro is the traffic replay under /opt/replays/draft-pairing/2026-03-17.tar.gz. key points: short prompts (<= 64 tokens), frequent model switching, and speculative acceptance tuned to 0.7. Attached the profiler snippet below.
maria: ```
TRACE: mixtral-v2 -> qwen-lite pairing
kernel: fused-attn-16b (selected)
seq_len: 32 -> 48
kv_cache_hits: 61% -> 20% (during switch windows)
batch_size: 4 -> 1 (rapid demotion)
latency_p95: 78ms -> 240ms
```
ash: hmm kernel selection seems fine initially. switching cost + tokenizer mismatch could be flushing kvs. what's tokenizer mismatch evidence?
liam: quick note — qwen-lite tokenizer respaces BOS/CLS differences. If the draft ended with a partial token boundary, acceptance heuristics fire and we attempt speculative finalize on a different tokenization grid, causing cache invalidation. Seen this on earlier qwen/mixtral pairings.
ash: can we instrument the handshake to log canonicalized token ids at the pairing boundary? if we see differing tokenization length or pretokenized bytes we can fast-fail speculative acceptance.
maria: added a lightweight probe to the runtime: `pairing-check --modelA mixtral-v2 --modelB qwen-lite --handshake-probe` — dump below sample:
```
PROBE 185678: draft_end_tokens: [1203, 54, 9] (len=3, bytes=7)
PROBE 185678: finalizer_start_tokens: [1203, 54, 10] (len=3, bytes=8)
DIFF: token_2 bytes mismatch -> kv key mismatch
```
liam: that's the smoking gun. token boundary differs by a single byte -> different token ids so KV cache keys don't align. Should we normalize to utf8-bytes or use canonical text normalization before forming KV keys?
ash: normalization is cheap but could shift other metrics. Alternative: at pairing handshake if canonicalized token sequence differs, mark as "soft-incompatible" and force model warmup (prefetch KV) instead of relying on speculative accept. That reduces latency benefits but prevents p95 spikes.
maria: agree. We should also detect when kernel-selected path depends on rope scaling assumptions. For mixtral we use RoPE scale 1.0; qwen-lite expects a 0.95 remap in earlier config which might change how attention offsets are hashed in kernel selector. If selector chooses kernel with different KV layout, warmup is mandatory.
ash: good point — kernel selection should include a pairing-compatibility check. I'll add a quick heuristic: require identical (heads, kv_dim, rope_scale) across pair or else treat as incompatible for zero-warmup speculative flow. That would be `if not compat -> batch_demote_to_warmup`.
liam: also saw batching behavior: when pairing causes batch_size to drop to 1 frequently, the kernel fused-attn-16b has poor per-token throughput. Maybe switch to `singlethreaded-attn` for batch1 to reduce context switch overhead.
maria: yes, and the runtime profiler suggests the scheduler demoted paired requests aggressively because acceptance callbacks blocked on tokenizer normalization RPC (~1.8ms). If we can inline a tiny canonicalizer (ascii/utf8 normalization) in the fast path we remove that RPC.
ash: plan of action: 1) add canonicalized-token handshake probe (cheap inline), 2) add pairing-compatibility check (heads/kv_dim/rope_scale), 3) fallback to warmup/prefetch on incompatible pairs, 4) add kernel override for batch==1 to `singlethreaded-attn`. I'll make a draft PR.
maria: pushing replay to the PR review so CI can run the bench.
benchmark-bot: Bench run queued: job id 88421 (mixtral-v2 + qwen-lite pairing)
benchmark-bot: initial results (replay v2026-03-17): baseline (speculative enabled) p95=240ms, after handshake-probe + warmup p95=92ms, delta: -148ms, cost +4% (extra warmup tokens).
ash: that's promising — reduces tail dramatically with small cost. We should add an opt-in flag `pairing.strict_compat=true` for Dedicated customers where latency SLO > cost sensitivity.
liam: one more tweak — acceptance_threshold 0.7 is too aggressive for cross-family pairing. Let's default to 0.85 for cross-family and keep 0.7 intra-family. That reduces harmful speculative commits.
maria: noted. I'll add config flags in `/etc/redwood/runtime/pairing.yaml` and stage rollout.
nash: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/pairs/merge/1127 — includes unit tests for tokenizer canonicalizer + benchmark script.
maria: will monitor next 24h after rollout. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: deploy started for pairing-compat-check (sha: a1b2c3) on cluster-3
maria: deploy looks green so far, p95 trending down to ~100ms. closing the thread if no more concerns.
liam: cheers
